clue.text: Slow-moving pair of tramps, each admitting cheeky love

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the two tramps take the cheeky love inside

parts.note: a tramp is a BUM, so a pair gives two of them
cheeky means pert, saucy
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
each is per, as in a pound per head

explanation.surface: Two vagrants dawdle along, each one making saucy advances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' signals containment: the cheeky love goes between the two tramps. 'each' looks like part of the picture but supplies the last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic described this way is nose to tail and crawling, an idiom for congestion.

clue.text: Double raise includes article to come last

indicators.note: includes means the two raises hold the article within them

parts.note: to raise a child is to bring up
to raise is also to rear
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A double lift takes in an item and finishes in final place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double raise' supplies two different synonyms of raise, and 'includes' puts the article between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up the rear is the idiom for being at the back of a procession, finishing last.

clue.text: Folk get on as trio somehow

definitions.text: Folk get on as trio somehow

parts.note: folk are people, men
to get on is to grow old, to age

indicators.note: somehow says these letters come out in some other order

explanation.surface: People rub along together as a threesome, one way or another.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer, a French phrase for a three-way household or relationship; AS TRIO rearranged gives the French word for three.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase names a domestic arrangement of three people in a sexual relationship, folk getting on as a trio.

clue.text: Knackered retina? Yes.

indicators.note: knackered means worn out or broken, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether their tired eye is the problem and is told it is.
explanation.walkthrough: A worn-out retina is just what the answer describes, so the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiredness of the eyes from overuse is what a knackered retina would suffer.

clue.text: Kind at first, then hardens and prepares for printing

parts.note: a kind is a type
concrete or jelly that hardens sets

explanation.surface: Someone is gentle at first, then turns tough, while getting a document ready for print.
explanation.definitionFit: Typesetting arranges text in type ready for the press, the step that readies copy for printing.

clue.text: White Christmas dreamer to stay at home holding hands

indicators.note: holding means the stay and the home wrap around the hands

parts.note: to stay is to be, to remain
at home is in
the two hands are right and left, R and L

explanation.surface: A songwriter who dreams of snow prefers to stay in, holding hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Irving Berlin wrote the song White Christmas, which opens 'I'm dreaming of a white Christmas'.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin wrote the song whose singer is dreaming of a white Christmas, so he is its dreamer.

clue.text: Deserve entire mark-up? No, just some of it

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top
just some of it says only a run of letters inside the phrase is used

explanation.surface: Does the whole price increase deserve it? No, only part of it does.
explanation.walkthrough: The run TIREM sits inside 'entire mark' and reads upwards; 'mark-up' looks like one word, but its 'up' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to deserve it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Grave words from some decrepit aphorist

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Solemn words come from an old, worn-out maker of sayings.
explanation.definitionFit: An inscription on a tombstone commemorates the dead, words on a grave.

clue.text: Legal officer accepts a right platter, served up by unknown vital supplier

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so the unknown comes next
accepts means the officer takes the other letters inside

parts.note: a coroner is a legal officer who investigates deaths

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means the platter reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a platter is a tray
Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A court official takes a dish served up by a mystery supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns the platter upwards in this down entry (YART); 'accepts' puts it, with A and R, inside the officer, and 'by' sets the unknown alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronary artery supplies blood to the heart muscle, a vital supply line.

clue.text: One putting up store in private

indicators.note: in places the store inside the word for private

parts.note: private thoughts are inner ones
to store is to keep

explanation.surface: Someone stockpiles goods in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One putting up' means one giving lodging, not one building or tolerating.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord of a tavern puts up guests overnight, giving them lodging.

clue.text: Perhaps one with horn

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A guess at someone who carries a horn, like a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: I and HORN rearranged give the animal; the whole clue also describes it, a beast with a horn on its snout.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal has one or two horns on its nose, so it is an example of one with horn.

clue.text: Concert to break a leg

parts.note: a gig is a concert

indicators.note: break says these two letters are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A performer is wished good luck before a concert: break a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface borrows the theatre wish 'break a leg', but 'break' works on TO and 'a leg' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigot is a leg of mutton or lamb, a cut of meat from the French.

clue.text: Mao and Stalin built walled city

indicators.note: built means the letters are constructed into a new form

explanation.surface: Two communist leaders put up a fortified town.
explanation.walkthrough: The names of the two dictators rearranged give the Breton port.
explanation.definitionFit: The Breton port is famous for its old town ringed by ramparts.

clue.text: Game not hard for the uneducated?

indicators.note: not means the hard letter is taken away

parts.note: pheasants are game birds
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A simple game, perhaps, for those with little schooling?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like a pastime but means game birds; the question mark marks the definition as loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural labourers of old were typically unschooled, so the poorest country folk stand for the uneducated.

clue.text: A maths problem gives rise to complaint

indicators.note: a problem is something worked out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tricky sum leaves someone grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' means an ailment, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronic breathing disorder is an ailment, and complaint is used for an illness.

clue.text: It cuts up apple crumble

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: cuts are axes, as in budget axes

indicators.note: crumble means the fruit is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A pudding instruction: chop the fruit and make a crumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts up' gives SEXA (AXES upwards); 'It' is old slang for allure, as in the It girl.
explanation.definitionFit: It was 1920s slang for personal magnetism and attractiveness, as in Clara Bow the It girl.

clue.text: A container in very good metal

indicators.note: in puts the container inside the word for very good

parts.note: a plum job is a very good one
a tin is a container

explanation.surface: A can stored inside a high-quality metal box.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum is a precious metallic element.

clue.text: We murmur a short reply

parts.note: to murmur is to hum

indicators.note: short means the reply is cut down to its opening letters

parts.note: a reply is an answer

explanation.surface: We mumble a brief response.
explanation.walkthrough: ANS is the usual short form of answer; the 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: We are people, members of the human race, so the pronoun stands for the species.

clue.text: 70% island drink

indicators.note: 70% means seven of the ten letters are kept from the front of the island's name

parts.note: Martinique is a Caribbean island

explanation.surface: A rum-strength drink from an island, at seventy per cent.
explanation.walkthrough: MARTINIQUE has ten letters, so 70% is its first seven.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: Supply cable possibly halved

parts.note: a flex is an electric cable

indicators.note: halved means only half of the word is kept, here the second half

parts.note: taken as written before halving

explanation.surface: A power cable for the supply may be cut in half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is the adverb from supple, not the noun or verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Supply is the adverb of supple, meaning in a bendy, pliant way.

clue.text: Second action plan in relation to plants

parts.note: B is second in order, as in plan B or a B-grade

indicators.note: plan means the letters are laid out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A backup course of action, plan B, applied to plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanic describes botany, the science of plants.

clue.text: Develop heart surgeon's material

indicators.note: heart means the middle letters of the word

parts.note: a vet is a veterinary surgeon

explanation.surface: A surgeon develops cloth for the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of DEVELOP is its middle three letters, VEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Velvet is a soft fabric with a short dense pile.

clue.text: Artist sanctuary's special delight

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a retreat is a sanctuary

explanation.surface: An artists' retreat is a special pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare treat is an unusual pleasure, special because uncommon.

clue.text: See 2
Dad's half-hearted spiel

indicators.note: half-hearted means one of the two central letters is lost

parts.note: a spiel is a patter

explanation.surface: Father gives a lukewarm sales pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: PATTER has a double T at its heart; dropping one halves it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pater is Latin for father, used in old-fashioned British slang for one's dad.

clue.text: Friend to travel on a motorway

indicators.note: on means the travel comes after the motorway

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, written MI
to travel is to go

explanation.surface: A friend set off along a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, its 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, used informally in English.

clue.text: With gene mutation in the lead, church gets retaliation

indicators.note: in places the mutated letters inside the lead

parts.note: in the van means in the lead, at the front

indicators.note: a mutation changes the order of the letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church takes revenge with a gene mutation leading the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutation' signals the anagram, making ENGE; 'in' sets that inside the word for the lead, from 'in the van', the front of an army.
explanation.definitionFit: Vengeance is punishment inflicted in return for a wrong.

clue.text: Fruit tickles my fancy: it's good for a starter

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or imaginative, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner enjoys a fruit starter that delights them.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a menu's first course; the starter is someone making a first attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said when a beginner succeeds on the first attempt, good fortune for a starter.
